sector: Courier, haulage, clearing and forwarding, and ocean shipping
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: Logistics firms sell movement and paperwork. Couriers charge per parcel by zone and weight; hauliers charge per trip by distance and load, then pay fuel, drivers, tolls and repairs out of it; clearing agents earn a fixed fee per container while passing the customer's duty straight to customs; shipping lines sell container slots in dollars. Margins are thin (5 to 10 percent), so profit comes from full trucks both ways, fast port clearance and well-kept vehicles.

caseStudies.scale: Revenue of $88.7bn in 2025 with an 8.9% GAAP operating margin; US revenue per piece up 8.3% in Q4 2025
caseStudies.lesson: Parcel profit is density: more pieces per stop and per route. UPS cut low-margin volume and raised revenue per piece. The game should reward dense zones and let players drop loss-making routes.

caseStudies.scale: Revenue of $12.0bn in 2025, operating income $865m (operating ratio about 92.8%); 2.14m intermodal loads at $2,795 each
caseStudies.lesson: Fuel is billed as a separate surcharge ($1.48bn in 2025), so fuel swings pass to customers. The game should show a fuel surcharge the player can set, and judge trucking by operating ratio.

caseStudies.scale: Over 160 service centres in 7 countries by mid-2026; 15 new centres and 70+ trucks added in H1 2026
caseStudies.lesson: Growth came from walk-in drop-off centres feeding a shared truck network, then e-commerce and cross-border lanes. The game should unlock new drop-off centres that feed one fleet.

caseStudies.scale: Listed on NGX; H1 2025 revenue N11.1bn (courier N5.2bn, freight N2.4bn); Q2 2025 operating margin about 5.8%
caseStudies.lesson: A Nigerian courier-plus-freight group runs on roughly 80% cost of sales and single-digit margins. The game should keep margins thin so efficiency, not price hikes, wins.

regulation.unitedStates: No federal courier licence for parcels; USPS keeps the letter monopoly. Truck operators register with FMCSA for a USDOT number.
regulation.nigeria: NIPOST licenses couriers by scope: municipal, state, regional, national, international. A 2020 fee rise (N250k SME to N20m) was suspended.

regulation.unitedStates: FMCSA: operating authority for for-hire carriers, 11-hour daily driving limit, electronic logging devices, drug and alcohol tests.
regulation.nigeria: FRSC driver licence classes and vehicle permits; NPA electronic call-up for trucks entering Lagos ports. No hard hours limit found.

regulation.unitedStates: CBP licenses customs brokers after an exam (19 CFR 111); brokers must keep responsible supervision and records.
regulation.nigeria: Nigeria Customs Service licenses customs agents under NCS Act 2023 s.103-107; renewal fees reviewed from January 2026.

regulation.unitedStates: Federal Maritime Commission rule (from 28 May 2024): invoice within 30 days, bill only shipper or consignee, 30 days to dispute.
regulation.nigeria: Nigerian Shippers' Council regulates charges, brokered longer free days, and orders refunds when carriers bill wrongly.

regulation.rule: Duty paid on the importer's behalf
regulation.unitedStates: CBP: importer of record owes duty and must post a customs bond; a broker may pay but the duty stays the importer's money.
regulation.nigeria: Nigeria Customs Service: duty paid through designated banks before release; false declaration brings penalties and seizure.

regulation.unitedStates: FMC licenses freight forwarders and NVOCCs (bond required) and polices carrier and terminal practices.
regulation.nigeria: Nigerian Ports Authority sets port dues; terminals charge storage; NSC registers shipping service providers.

gameRules.name: Route pricing
gameRules.rule: List price: bike = N1,500 + N500 x zone (1-5); waybill = N5,000 + N4 x km; 40ft trip = N1,200,000 + N1,900 x km. Player sets -20% to +20%; demand falls 1.5% per 1% above list, rises 1% per 1% below.
gameRules.playerFeels: Long routes pay more, but greedy pricing empties the drop-off yard.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Zone and distance tariffs used by Lagos couriers and Lagos-Kano haulage quotes

gameRules.name: Fuel cost per trip
gameRules.rule: Fuel = km driven x 0.45 L/km x diesel price (start N1,650/L, daily move +/-3%, bounds N1,300-2,300). Both legs always burn fuel. Fuel surcharge toggle adds (price-1,650)/1,650 x 30% to quotes.
gameRules.playerFeels: Diesel news matters; a surcharge protects margin but annoys some customers.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NBS diesel N1,648/L (Mar 2026), Nigerian fuel share 35-45%, J.B. Hunt fuel surcharge

gameRules.name: Fill the return trip
gameRules.rule: Chance of a backhaul = 30% + 10% per depot level at destination + 15% if player visited that city this week, cap 85%. Backhaul pays 50% of outbound price. Empty return earns N0 and still burns fuel.
gameRules.playerFeels: An empty truck coming home hurts; a found return load feels like a win.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: ATRI 16.7% empty miles in the US; Kobo360-style load matching in Nigeria

gameRules.name: Demurrage clock
gameRules.rule: Each import box gets 5 free days from berthing. Then N13,000/day days 6-10, N19,000 days 11-15, N26,000 after. Customer is billed; if delay is the player's paperwork, player pays 50%. Trust -2 per day past free.
gameRules.playerFeels: A ticking timer on every box; clearing fast is the job.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Hapag-Lloyd Nigeria 40ft tariff: 5-7 free days then N9,500-26,100/day

gameRules.name: Duty held for customers
gameRules.rule: Duty = cargo value x class rate (5, 10, 20 or 35%) +7.5% VAT. Customer pays it into a locked Duty Pot, not player cash; job waits if pot is short. Income is the N250,000 fee only. 1 in 10 boxes inspected; wrong class = N500,000 fine+3 days.
gameRules.playerFeels: Big money passes through your hands but is never yours; honesty is safe.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Agents pay duty for importers via NCS banks; misdeclaration penalties under NCS Act 2023

gameRules.name: Fleet maintenance
gameRules.rule: Each vehicle has condition 100. Truck -1 per 250 km, bike -1 per 60 km. Service: truck N180,000, bike N15,000, restores 100. Below 60, breakdown chance per trip = (60 - condition)%. Breakdown: 2 days lost, N450,000 repair, trust -5.
gameRules.playerFeels: Skipping service saves cash today and costs a stranded load tomorrow.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: ATRI repair cost $0.22/mile rising 8.6%; Nigerian road wear raises breakdown risk

gameRules.name: Rider share
gameRules.rule: Hired riders keep 70% of each delivery fee; player keeps 30%. Player delivering personally keeps 100% but cannot run stations meanwhile. Rider trust bonus +1 per 50 safe deliveries; speeding is never rewarded.
gameRules.playerFeels: Hiring trades margin for scale and time.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Lagos couriers take 60-75% of the delivery fee

gameRules.name: Operating ratio gate
gameRules.rule: Operating ratio = monthly costs / monthly revenue x 100, excluding duty passed to customs. Bank truck or ship loans need ratio under 95 for 3 straight months. Under 90 earns a 1-point lower interest rate.
gameRules.playerFeels: A single number tells the player if the business is healthy.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Trucking firms are judged by operating ratio: J.B. Hunt 92.8%, Red Star about 94%

uniqueMechanics.name: Route and return-load board
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Picks a destination for each truck, sees fuel cost and price before dispatch, and taps waiting backhaul offers in the destination city to fill the trip home.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Nigeria map with truck icons, route cost/price card, and a list of return loads per city

uniqueMechanics.name: Demurrage clock wall
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Watches every import box count down its free days, prioritises paperwork for the reddest boxes, and decides which to clear first when the desk is busy.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Port yard grid with a coloured day counter on each container and a daily charge preview

uniqueMechanics.name: Duty Pot ledger
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Takes customer duty deposits into a locked pot, picks the correct goods class for each declaration, and pays customs from the pot; only the fee lands in cash.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Two-column ledger: locked Duty Pot vs business cash, with a declaration form and class picker

failureStates.trigger: Truck condition under 60 breaks down (chance = 60 minus condition, in %)
failureStates.consequence: 2 days lost, N450,000 repair, trust -5, contract client may leave at trust under 40
failureStates.recovery: Send a rescue van, pay the repair, then service the whole fleet to 100

failureStates.trigger: 5 or more boxes past free days at once, or one box past 15 days
failureStates.consequence: Daily charges reach N26,000 per box, trust -2 per box per day, importers move to a rival
failureStates.recovery: Hire a second licensed agent or upgrade the paperwork desk; clear the oldest box first

failureStates.trigger: Diesel above N2,000/L for 7 days with no fuel surcharge and ratio above 100
failureStates.consequence: Each trip loses money; bank loan gate closes
failureStates.recovery: Switch on fuel surcharge, cut empty returns, park the oldest truck

failureStates.trigger: A box inspected (1 in 10) with the wrong goods class
failureStates.consequence: N500,000 fine paid from player cash, 3-day hold, trust -10
failureStates.recovery: Re-declare correctly, pay the fine, and pass a declaration training task

balanceNotes: Payback in game months: stage 1 about 2, stage 2 about 5, stage 3 about 13, stage 4 about 14, stage 5 about 27, stage 6 about 11, stage 7 about 22, stage 8 about 28. Players will feel stuck at Big Wheels and the Warehouse Years: trucks and warehouses are costly and margins are only 6 to 10%. Tune first the backhaul chance and the diesel start price, then the warehouse startup cost. Keep the duty pot outside every profit figure.
openQuestions: Storyline says 3 free days and N40,000/day demurrage; research shows 5-7 days and N9,500-26,100. Which do we use?
Should the fuel surcharge be automatic or a player choice that costs some demand?
How many real minutes is one game day, so the 5-day demurrage clock feels tense but fair?
Is buying a ship (N25bn) the endgame, or should chartering stay the main path?
